turns.learner: Hello! I have an English exam soon. Can we practise going to for plans?
turns.tutor:
Good idea before an exam. Quick question first: what is one thing you plan to do this weekend? Think about it, we will build on it.

Here is a worked example (my own example):
I want to say a plan: "my sister / cook / dinner / tonight".
Step 1: The subject is "my sister", so I use "is".
Step 2: After "is going to" the verb stays in its base form: cook.
Step 3: I keep the time word: tonight.
Result: "My sister is going to cook dinner tonight."

Now you try a partly solved one. Step 1 is done: the subject is "we", so we use "are".
"We ___ ___ ___ (paint) the office next week."
Write the three missing words.
